q: why do some people have a musical ear
why can some people sing in key
why do some people struggle to stay on key
a: Musical ear (the ability to perceive, produce, and differentiate musical pitch) varies significantly among individuals due to a combination of genetic and environmental factors. Perfect pitch (absolute pitch) is the ability to identify or produce a musical note without any reference tone. It occurs in about 1 in 10,000 people and has a strong genetic component, though early musical training before age 6 significantly increases the likelihood. Relative pitch, the ability to identify intervals between notes, is much more common and can be developed through training. Tone deafness (amusia) affects about 4% of the population and is a neurological condition where the brain has difficulty processing pitch differences. It is not related to hearing ability but to how the brain processes sound. Studies of identical twins suggest that musical aptitude is about 50% heritable. Early exposure to music and training can significantly improve pitch perception and vocal accuracy through neuroplasticity. Most people who think they are tone deaf can actually improve significantly with practice and ear training exercises.
